title: The Chord That Opens the Cavern
story: Deep beneath the hills lies a cathedral of singing crystals, and behind its locked gate wait three lost cave-mapmakers. Hushclaver the Chord Warden hovers before the gate and hums the rule: the gate opens only when five crystals are struck and their hums AVERAGE exactly 12 tones. Mr 6 has already struck four crystals, and the Warden grins, sure that no six-shaped knight can do arithmetic under pressure.
question: The first four crystals hummed 9, 15, 10, and 12 tones. How many tones must the fifth crystal hum so that the five hums average exactly 12?
solution: To average 12 across 5 crystals, the hums must total 12 × 5 = 60 tones.
The four struck crystals gave 9 + 15 + 10 + 12 = 46 tones.
So the last crystal must hum 60 - 46 = 14 tones.
praise: Adding the four hums was the perfect first move — the step still waiting was turning the target average into a target TOTAL (12 × 5).
hint: An average of 12 across 5 crystals means a certain total. What total would that have to be?
victory: Mr 6 tapped the fifth crystal for a ringing 14, the chord landed dead on average, and Hushclaver popped like a soap bubble of sound — the mapmakers walked out humming the tune all the way home.
imagePrompt: A glowing underground cathedral of tall humming crystals in blue and violet light, a translucent robed warden hovering before a sealed stone gate while a small numeral-6 knight raises his sword to tap a crystal.
